audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Blinding Dart 'erases Yone's first Q dash trade' and that under the blind 'his Spirit Cleave auto-component whiffs' / 'Spirit Cleave loses its auto-component'. Neither is true.
audit.why: The wiki's Mortal Steel interaction list reads 'Blind: both first target and secondary target take damage' — Q lands through Blind exactly as Yasuo's does. Spirit Cleave is a cone ability that deals part physical and part magic damage and shields him; it has no basic-attack component and no Blind interaction at all. Blind only removes his actual autos and the Way of the Hunter magic hit riding every second one.
audit.corrected: Blind takes his basic attacks and the passive on-hit. Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave both land through it — spacing and the W shield timer are what you actually play around.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave's shield is never mentioned in either layer, only its damage.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave shields him for an amount that grows with champions hit, and its cooldown scales down with his bonus attack speed. Against a poke lane that shield is the thing eating your Toxic Shot chip — every W he casts on the wave refunds part of your poke, which is why a Teemo who trades on cooldown rather than on his W timer never builds a lead.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave shields him and its cooldown shortens as he buys attack speed — poke into the gap after he spends it on the wave, not into a fresh one.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say 'track Soul Unbound' without a number, and content.mid tells you to trade 'when his Soul Unbound timer is visible'.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1 dropping to 10 at rank 5 — a genuinely huge early window. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, so at rank 1 of his E you get three darts per Soul Unbound. That is the sequencing line the entry was missing.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1 to 10s at rank 5; Fate Sealed 120/100/80s; your dart is flat 7s. Three darts per rank-1 E.

audit.why: Fate Sealed is described in the entry as a knockup, and the wiki confirms it stuns, pulls, then knocks up for 0.75s — so that claim stands and was left alone.

edits.before: Blinding Shot already erases Yone's first Q dash trade — he auto-attacks into a miss window and takes full poison-on-hit damage for free.
edits.after: Blinding Dart takes Yone's autos and his passive on-hit, but Mortal Steel lands through Blind — the free chip is real, the free Q window is not.

edits.after: Blind his basic attacks and the Way of the Hunter on-hit — Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave both land regardless, so space instead

edits.before: Stack Spirit Cleave hits in melee range where your Move Quick burst cannot fully disengage before the cleave connects
edits.after: Cast Spirit Cleave in melee for the shield that refunds your poke, where Move Quick cannot fully disengage first

edits.before: Yone has no ranged poke at Level 1 and his Q dash auto-follow misses into Blinding Shot — land the blind on his first approach and the poke lead is yours immediately.
edits.after: Yone has no ranged poke at Level 1 and Blinding Dart removes his autos and passive on-hit — but not Mortal Steel, so take the free chip and hold your spacing.

edits.before: A maxed Blinding Shot on a four-second cooldown blankets every wave trade: he can never auto freely, Spirit Cleave loses its auto-component, and mushrooms cover both approach paths.
edits.after: A maxed Blinding Dart on a flat 7 seconds blankets every wave: he never autos freely. Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave still land, so poke into the gap right after he spends W on the wave.

edits.after: Fate Sealed becomes a real threat at Level 6 — he can chain R into Soul Unbound for a kill combo, and E is 22 seconds at rank 1, so you get three darts per cast if you count it.

edits.before: Yone wants to walk up, Q-dash twice, and trade with Spirit Cleave autos — Blinding Shot dismantles that entire pattern. The moment his first Q animation fires, hit him with Q: his autos miss, his Spirit Cleave auto-component whiffs, and your Toxic Shot poison ticks on him for free. He has no reliable poke of his own at Level 1, so you set the tone immediately. Keep Move Quick charged by avoiding damage in between skirmishes — when he burns Soul Unbound to escape, the doubled movement speed lets you chase the rewind path and land one more poison auto before he snaps back.
edits.after: Yone wants to walk up, Q twice and trade with Spirit Cleave — Blinding Dart dents that pattern without dismantling it. The blind removes his basic attacks and the Way of the Hunter magic hit riding every second one, and that is real free damage. What it does not remove is Mortal Steel or Spirit Cleave: the wiki lists Q as landing through Blind, and W is a cone ability with no auto component at all. So blind his walk-up, take the chip, and hold spacing for the Q. Keep Move Quick charged by avoiding damage between skirmishes — when he burns Soul Unbound, the speed lets you land one more poison auto before he snaps back.

edits.before: With Q maxed and shrooms sealing the tribush and jungle entrances, Yone cannot approach without walking into a slow-and-reveal field. Trade on every wave: poke, W back out, re-poison, repeat. His biggest window here is Fate Sealed — the R knockup is lethal if he catches you flat-footed in the open, so never stand in a straight line between him and your tower. Pre-shroom the path he will dash along and he will be slowed mid-animation, giving Move Quick time to widen the gap before he completes the engage. At Level 6 his threat spikes because Fate Sealed charges faster, so treat this as the cautious phase: maintain a shroom screen and only trade when his Soul Unbound timer is visible and committed.
edits.after: With Q maxed and shrooms sealing the tribush and jungle entrances, Yone cannot approach without walking into a slow-and-reveal field. Trade on his W timer, not on yours: Spirit Cleave shields him and its cooldown shortens as he buys attack speed, so poke into the gap right after he spends it clearing the wave. His biggest window here is Fate Sealed — the R stuns, pulls, then knocks up, and it is lethal if it catches you flat-footed, so never stand in a straight line between him and your tower. Pre-shroom the path he dashes along and he is slowed mid-animation, giving Move Quick time to widen the gap. Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1 against your flat 7-second dart — count it and you get three blinds per cast.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — He snaps back when it ends. Shroom there. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yone Soul Unbound: 22s at rank 1 to 10s at rank 5 — he snaps back when it ends, so shroom there. Your dart is flat 7s: three per rank-1 E. - Fate Sealed: 120/100/80s. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Q-blind erases his auto-trade window entirely. Only take the trade when Yone's Soul Unbound is down.
edits.after: Q-blind erases his autos and passive on-hit, not Mortal Steel. Trade when Soul Unbound is down.

edits.before: AA Yone on every last-hit, Q-blind his trade attempt, and walk the poison out of his reach.
edits.after: AA on every last-hit and Q-blind his walk-up — but Mortal Steel still lands, so hold your spacing.

notes: Same Blind finding as the Yasuo entry: the wiki's Mortal Steel interaction list reads 'Blind: both first target and secondary target take damage', so Yone's Q is not stopped by Blinding Dart. Separately, the entry called Spirit Cleave an auto-attack in three places — it is a cone ability with no basic-attack component, so Blind does nothing to it and it also shields him, which neither layer mentioned. Fate Sealed being a knockup was checked and is correct (stun, then pull, then a 0.75s knock-up), so it was left unchanged.
